personas.name: Platform Admin

businessRules.rule: A skill version never changes once saved. A draft is a separate record and does not change a published Playbook.
businessRules.appliesTo: Pin a skill version at publish

businessRules.rule: A preset update reaches a draft only after someone accepts the diff. Publish does not pick up a new preset version on its own.
businessRules.appliesTo: Review a preset update before publish

businessRules.rule: Instruction files are part of the published bundle hash. Reference files are read at their latest approved version when a run starts, once for that run.
The author of a reference-file version cannot approve it. A fork cannot be published while a capability or skill-type change is unapproved.
A new project skill cannot declare capabilities. A new publish names a skill version. A bare repo path is accepted only from a Playbook published before Part 3.
An interactive step resumes only after the assignee approves output that passes the loose result and the skill's kind. Cancelling the run records no result.

features.title: Versioned skills that published Playbooks pin
features.description: Project Admins publish a Playbook against a skill version. A later preset edit becomes a new version a draft can review, and Playbooks already published keep running.
outOfScope: The Skill Library page
Interactive agent chat

items.title: Store immutable skill versions and pin them at publish
items.description: Add the skill version store for presets, forks, project skills, and companion files. Parse skill frontmatter as YAML, copy type and kind to columns, and hash the skill version plus instruction files. Publish freezes that version. A run of a Part 3 policy checks the bundle hash. A run of an older policy checks the single-file hash and is never rehashed. Reference files stay out of the hash. A preset is keyed by its frontmatter name, with a rename map so a renamed preset continues. After Part 3, a new publish names a skill version.
technicalDependencies: Playbook publish and the current agent-run policy
The background agent worker that checks the skill hash
nonFunctionalRequirements: Saving a version and resolving it at publish stays within 2 seconds at P95
Two saves cannot overwrite a stored version
definitionOfDone: A published Playbook still runs after the preset file on disk changes, and the run uses the pinned bytes.
An instruction-file change is not visible to a published Playbook until that Playbook is republished.
A second preset source with an existing preset key is refused.
A node with a kind is checked against the loose result first and the kind second. A node with no kind keeps today's loose check.

items.title: Import current skills without breaking published Playbooks
items.description: Run the production inventory first and attach it to the change. It lists every pinned skill path and hash, every incident policy missing the cloud-shell capability, and every project whose published Playbook uses the incident skill. Import those bytes as version 1 before any skill file is edited. On startup, insert a new preset version when a preset source hash is new, including the renamed project-neutral incident skill as version 2 of the same preset. Map the three old incident paths to that version 1 entry and compare the path string the policy froze. Point the recommender at the new incident path and remove only the worker's old-name shell check. Record the shell capability on any version 1 incident entry whose frozen policy lacks it. Import the MaxView catalog as MaxView's first approved reference file. Pause incident schedules in any other project until that project has a reader identity. Carry the project's reader client ID on the run specification. The worker has no fallback identity.
technicalDependencies: Production Playbook versions for the inventory
Git history of the current skill files
nonFunctionalRequirements: The startup import runs on one instance at a time
A preset source over 200,000 bytes is skipped, logged, and does not create a version
definitionOfDone: The migration does not merge until the inventory is attached.
A published incident Playbook runs against its version 1 bytes after the preset is renamed.
Drafts of that preset show a reviewable diff and nothing is republished automatically.
The SkillOpt plan is renumbered to Part 4 in its own doc edit.
An incident run in a project with no reader identity fails with a clear message instead of using another project's identity.

items.title: Enforce library permissions and reference-file rules
items.description: Add the view and reference-approval permissions, and start checking the existing manage permission. Review who already holds that permission, globally and per project. A project role overrides a global role. The library menu appears only where Playbooks are enabled. Reference-file contents require author or approver permission. Generate and save reject capabilities, a reference-file key, invalid YAML, an unknown kind, and invalid decision labels. Names are unique in the project and cannot reuse a preset key. A project file whose name matches a preset file is rejected. A fork cannot change which files are reference files. A fork with a capability or skill-type change cannot be published until a Platform Admin approves it.
technicalDependencies: The existing role and menu-visibility checks
nonFunctionalRequirements: A library list returns within 2 seconds at P95
Reference-file contents are omitted from view-only responses
definitionOfDone: A view-only user can read instruction files and reference-file names, and cannot read reference-file contents.
The author of a reference-file version cannot approve it, and a Platform Admin cannot approve their own edit.
The library warns when fewer than two people in the project can approve.
A generated draft is not saved until the author saves it, and the author is recorded.
A Playbook author without the skill-view permission still sees names, types, and kinds in the builder picker.

items.title: Run interactive turns under the published policy
items.description: Register the interactive step as leaving Apex, with the same read-only profile refusal as a background agent step. Give it a frozen policy and a hash check. Each turn runs as a Playbook agent run on the step's thread and is admitted and spend-checked on its own. The step counts once toward the agent-step cap. The deadline matches the interview step. The assignee is notified when the step opens and 24 hours before it expires. Cancelling the run aborts an in-flight turn and closes the thread without deleting it. A triggered Playbook cannot be published when this step has no assignee.
technicalDependencies: The Playbook step registry and the approval-gate check
The existing chat session hook used by other agent surfaces
nonFunctionalRequirements: No agent run is in flight while the step waits for the assignee
A denied turn does not consume a hidden retry
definitionOfDone: A read-only interactive step needs no approval gate. A write profile is refused.
A proposal that fails either schema is retried out of view at most twice, then the assignee is told and can keep chatting.
Reaching the turn limit forces one proposal. After one rejected revision, the assignee can only approve or cancel.
When the deadline passes, the step expires and the run ends with no partial result.
The assignee is notified in the app and in Teams, and the notification opens the run.

items.title: Approve an interactive agent result

nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Sending a chat turn shows progress within 1 second and does not block the rest of the run view.
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: The chat, the approve action, and the cancel action are keyboard reachable and named for a screen reader.
nonFunctionalRequirements.security: The assignee must still be allowed to run Playbooks in the project when the step starts. Someone who lost access fails the step instead of leaving it waiting.

implementationPhases.rationale: There is one epic. FEAT-001 is the version store the library and the interactive step both pin. FEAT-002 and FEAT-003 depend on it and can proceed after that store exists. They do not depend on each other.

assumptionsMade: The accepted ADR "Playbooks Part 3: Skill Library and Skill Contracts" is the scope. This PRD does not add decisions.
Playbooks menu visibility stays the way a project turns Playbooks on. The library does not need its own flag.
MaxView already has a reader identity. Part 3 records it and does not create identities.
The production inventory is a gate for the migration, and its results are not known yet. The allow-list of preset paths outside the foundation folder grows from that inventory.
Each interactive turn runs as a Playbook agent run on the step's thread, not through the Agent Home chat path.
A Playbook author sees skill names, types, and kinds in the builder without the skill-view permission.
